lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding

nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 fixed a review round 1 CRITICAL finding: the per-respawn resolver self-invoke command built at setupPanes (src/commands/run.ts:627, `${q(process.execPath)} ${q(process.argv[1] ?? 'cam')} orch-resolve`) was invalid on the compiled distribution cam actually ships (`bun build --compile`, scripts/build-release.sh) -- inside a compiled single-file executable process.argv[1] is bun's internal virtual embedded-entry path (observed as `/$bunfs/root/<outfile>` on bun 1.3.13), and passing it back into argv makes the SAME binary's own `main()` command dispatch (argv[2]) print `unknown command: /$bunfs/root/<outfile>` and exit 1, while `<bin> orch-resolve` (no second token) works. Every US-003 installed-binary session therefore silently fell into the fail-safe fallback branch on EVERY respawn (re-using the build-time model/effort forever + one orch-resolve-fallback event per respawn), defeating US-003's whole acceptance criterion on the shipped path; only `bun index.ts run` (interpreted dev mode) worked correctly. Fix: extracted a new pure exported helper `resolveOrchResolverCmd(execPath: string, argv1: string | undefined): string` (src/commands/run.ts, next to the `q()` helper) that detects compiled mode via EITHER of two independent signals (defense in depth against a future bun version changing the virtual path's exact prefix) -- `argv1` starting with `/$bunfs/`, OR `basename(execPath) !== 'bun'` (a compiled binary's execPath is the binary itself, never named `bun`) -- and in that case renders `${q(execPath)} orch-resolve` (execPath alone, no second argv token); otherwise it keeps the pre-existing `${q(execPath)} ${q(argv1 ?? 'cam')} orch-resolve` shape (interpreted-mode self-invoke, or the bare `'cam' orch-resolve` PATH-lookup fallback when argv1 is genuinely absent). The `setupPanes` call site now reads `const resolverCmd = resolveOrchResolverCmd(process.execPath, process.argv[1]);` instead of inlining the broken template. `buildOrchestratorPaneCommand`'s own `resolverCmd?: string` option and its default (bare `'cam orch-resolve'`) are UNCHANGED -- this fix only touches how the real `setupPanes` caller assembles the string it passes in, never the builder's pure-string-assembly contract. Tests: test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts adds (a) 4 pure unit tests on resolveOrchResolverCmd covering interpreted mode, both compiled-mode detection signals independently, and the argv1-absent interpreted fallback, and (b) one end-to-end wiring test that monkeypatches `process.execPath`/`process.argv[1]` around a real `runRun(...)` call (both are plain writable properties on Bun 1.3.13, confirmed via `bun -e`) and asserts the resolverCmd actually embedded in the dispatched orchestrator pane argv (captured via the fake tmux spawn, same convention as test/commands/run-configpath-seam.test.ts) matches the collapsed compiled-mode shape with no `bunfs` substring anywhere in the dispatched command. `forkMonitor` (src/retry/launcher.ts) shares the IDENTICAL `[process.execPath, process.argv[1] ?? 'cam', ...subcommand]` self-invoke convention and therefore likely carries the SAME latent bug on a compiled binary, but it was deliberately left untouched: the reviewer finding named only the `orch-resolve` call site, and touching `forkMonitor` would widen this story's diff beyond its acceptance criteria (Surgical Changes) -- flagging it here as a plausible, not-yet-filed follow-up for whoever next touches retry/rate-limit self-invoke logic. src/commands/run.ts crossed 1127->1165 lines, raised with a tracker-ref-carrying `_ref` entry in scripts/file-size-budget.json (per-story rubric: only this file's own ceiling was raised, no other budgeted file touched).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Bun's official single-file-executable docs confirm compiled executables use a virtual filesystem with the `/$bunfs/` path prefix for embedded assets, resolved from the embedded StandaloneModuleGraph rather than the real filesystem at runtime -- consistent with the reviewer's empirical probe (`/$bunfs/root/<outfile>` observed as process.argv[1] inside a bun-1.3.13-compiled binary). The docs do not explicitly document process.argv[1]/process.execPath's exact runtime values inside a compiled executable (that specific behavior remains empirically-verified, not officially documented), so the fix deliberately does not rely on the bunfs-prefix signal ALONE: it is OR'd with `basename(execPath) !== 'bun'`, a signal that is directly implied by the docs' own framing of a compiled executable as bundling "the Bun runtime into a single executable file" (i.e. execPath is necessarily the standalone binary itself, not a separately-invoked bun runtime named 'bun').
